findings.spec: FR-9: 'a request counts from the first time it may have reached the customer to the last'
findings.summary: An email retried through an outage whose final send may have gone out (an ambiguous error that is not retried) is marked failed with sent_at cleared. askedRecently's upper bound, greatest(sent_at, maybe_sent_at, scheduled_for), then fell back to when that retry was due, not when it went out. If the send job ran late (up to the 20-hour retry window), the customer could be asked again before 90 days from that last send.
findings.evidence: Regression test 'counts a retried email to its last possible send, even when that send ran late': retry due 17:15Z, sent at 22:15Z, a new visit due 1 hour before 90 days after 22:15Z was scheduled instead of skipped as duplicate (failed on 9d771e1, passes with the fix).
findings.fix: deliver() sets scheduled_for to the send time when it fails a send that may have reached the customer (not when the provider refused it). scheduled_for of a failed row is read only by askedRecently.
tests_added: counts a retried email to its last possible send, even when that send ran late
does not extend the window to a final send the provider refused

observations.summary: The upper bound uses scheduled_for, so a row that was rescheduled (an email retry or a send-window deferral) and then skipped or expired before that send is counted until the planned time, at most about 20 hours past its last possible send (the email retry window). This only ever skips, never adds, an ask, within a 90-day window.

recordJobRun keeps a stored last_run_at that is up to 1 hour ahead of a new run, and jobsStatus ignores times ahead of now. After a clock running ahead writes a row, GET /api/status/jobs can show that job as never run or late for up to an hour. The result is a false alarm, not a missed one. Vercel clocks are NTP-synced, so this is not expected in practice.

observations.status: open (unconfirmed; not reproducible with real Twilio behaviour)
observations.summary: recordDelivery takes a per-request lock and recordSmsFailure takes the location lock. If a 'delivered' and an 'undelivered' receipt for the same SID arrived at the same moment, both could apply: the text would count as delivered and the request would also go by email. Twilio sends one final status per message, so this was not reproduced.
